subject: Post-call recap: volume discount vs latency trade-offs & pilot next steps
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@cobaltpayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: volume discount vs latency trade-offs & pilot next steps

Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain / goals you shared:
- Token spend is the largest line item for the fraud-screening service at Cobalt once you hit 5M monthly decisions. Current infra team projected a 3–4x cost increase if you go to a 1s latency SLO on Monday peak loads.
- Primary goal is to reduce unit cost (tokens per decision) without increasing tail latency above 1.2s at 99th percentile.
- Compliance: customer data cannot leave your VPC for pilot; you need audit log exports and basic KMS integration.
- Budget constraint: Q4 pilot budget is $65k–$85k (noted by procurement).

What we recommended on the call (short):
- Intelligent batching + adaptive prefix caching: expected 25–40% token reduction on decision traffic with minimal median latency impact.
- Quantized model variant for background scoring (lower-cost path) + single-token fallback to full model for uncertain cases. This hybrid reduces unit cost but introduces a small 2–3% change to model outputs — we’ll validate via your evaluation set.
- Dedicated pool (reserved) for peak windows to control latency and get improved per-token pricing (volume discount).
- Private deployment in your VPC for the pilot to satisfy compliance + KMS audit logs export.

Initial ballpark economics (illustrative; see attached pricing model):
- Baseline: current spend estimate $120k/month at current throughput assumptions.
- Pilot target (3-week): show 30% unit cost reduction -> equivalent run-rate ~$84k/month.
- If peak-tail remains within 1.2s P99 and quality delta <1.5% on your eval set, recommended commit: 6–12 month reserved to capture volume discounts.

Open questions we need to close to size pilot/SOW:
1) Accurate monthly decision volume (peak minute and 95th percentile QPS). Jordan mentioned 5M/month estimate — can you share last 30 days traffic snapshot or a CSV export?
2) Representative prompt/decision lengths (avg tokens in + avg tokens out).
3) Any disallowed external egress patterns for the pilot (we understand VPC-only for sensitive flows).
4) Procurement contact(s) for an SOW and timing constraints (Ava included).

Mutual action plan / next steps (owners & timing):
- Cobalt (Jordan/Ava): provide traffic CSV + anonymized eval set by Thu Oct 7.
- Redwood (Mina): deliver a tailored pilot proposal, SOW draft, and an anonymized cost model (attachments) by Mon Oct 4.
- Redwood (Karthik): quick feasibility check on batching/lib changes needed to hit 1.2s P99 with adaptive batching by Fri Oct 1.
- Joint: 30–45 minute pilot review + decision call the week of Oct 11.

Attachments: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (cost scenarios), pilot-size-assumptions.pdf (sizing assumptions & validators).

If that looks right I’ll route the SOW to Ava and lock k8s/VPC onboarding slots for the week of Oct 18.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: pilot-size-assumptions.pdf (pdf)]

-----Original Message-----
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@cobaltpayments.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava R. <procurement@cobaltpayments.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: volume discount vs latency trade-offs & pilot next steps

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- We can definitely provide the last 30 days traffic CSV (will strip PII). Should have that by EOD Thu Oct 7 as requested.
- On latency: 1.2s P99 is the hard ceiling for decisioning impacts to our user flows. Anything above that on a sustained basis requires product signoff.
- Procurement: Ava is copied; our Q4 budget window is tight. If Redwood can show a credible run-rate and a clear commit-to-discount path, we’ll try to accelerate approvals.

Also — can you prepare an anonymized example showing how batching would behave under our peak waveform (we’ll share a sample minute-by-minute CSV)? That will help our infra team.

Jordan
VP, Product — Cobalt Payments

-----On Thu, Sep 30, 2026 at 17:10 Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: volume discount vs latency trade-offs & pilot next steps

Mina — quick note from infra feasibility review:
- Adaptive batching with their signal profile is doable without codegen-level changes; we’ll need a short tuning window in staging (2–3 days) to tune batch timeouts to hit 1.2s P99.
- KV prefix caching should be implemented as a request-level cache in front of the model; ops effort ~1.5 engineer days + config for cache invalidation rules.
- Dedicated pool sizing: recommend we propose a small reserved pool (2 x A100-equivalent) for peak windows to start; we can autoscale to burst capacity if needed.

I’ll draft the ops section for the SOW and link the staging checklist.
—Karthik

If procurement prefers, I can also put together a 1-pager that maps the ROI to their budgeting line items for faster signoff. Would that help?

Best —
Mina
